raw_case_text:
In November 2005, a 78-year-old man with underlying rheumatoid arthritis was sent to the emergency department with generalized weakness and poor appetite of several weeks' duration. He had received oral therapy with prednisolone (5 mg twice per day), hydroxychloroquine (200 mg twice per day), sulfasalazine (1,000 mg twice per day), and methotrexate (MTX) (15 mg per week) for 4 months. The patient's body temperature was 38.5 C, blood pressure was 129/80 mm Hg, pulse rate was 76 beats/min, and respiratory rate was 20 breaths/min. Physical examination disclosed mild icteric sclera and multiple ecchymosis on the extremities.
A complete blood cell count showed a leukocyte count of 6,110/muL (4% bands, 77% segmented neutrophils, 7% lymphocytes, 6% normoblasts, and 3% myelocytes), hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 3,000/muL. Biochemical testing showed total bilirubin level of 3.89 mg/dL (normal 0-1.3 mg/dL) and alkaline phosphatase level of 480 U/L (60-220 U/L). Renal function, liver enzymes, and electrolyte levels were all within normal limits. The rheumatoid factor level was 76.3 IU/mL (normal <15 IU/mL). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level were 30 mm/hour (0-20 mm/hour) and 100 mg/L (0-5 mg/L), respectively. Test results for HIV and antinuclear antibody were negative. A chest radiograph showed bilateral interstitial micronodules and a fibrocalcified pattern. Abdominal ultrasonography indicated splenomegaly. The patient was admitted with the tentative diagnosis of MTX-induced thrombocytopenia.
Bone marrow aspiration (Figure 1) and biopsy were performed because of refractory thrombocytopenia and the presence of young blood cells on the peripheral blood smears. Intravenous amphotericin B (0.7 mg/kg/day) was administered because disseminated histoplasmosis was highly suspected because of the bone marrow findings. Four weeks later, the fungal culture of the bone marrow showed growth of mold (Figure 2A and B). The microorganism was subsequently identified as H. capsulatum by PCR assay (Figure 2C). No H. capsulatum was cultured from the patient's peripheral blood and sputum.
The patient's general condition improved after administration of a total dose of 1 g of intravenous amphotericin B, and the patient was discharged and treated with oral itraconazole, 200 mg once a day. Two weeks later, itraconazole therapy was suspended because impaired liver function was found. The patient was closely monitored for 3 months, and no clinical evidence of histoplasmosis relapse was noted.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 78-year-old man with rheumatoid arthritis presented with generalized weakness and poor appetite of several weeks' duration.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In November 2005, the patient developed progressive generalized weakness and anorexia over several weeks after receiving immunosuppressive therapy (prednisolone, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine, and methotrexate) for rheumatoid arthritis for 4 months.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized weakness and poor appetite. Home medications (for 4 months): prednisolone 5 mg BID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, sulfasalazine 1,000 mg BID, and methotrexate 15 mg weekly.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: temperature 38.5 C, BP 129/80 mmHg, HR 76 beats/min, RR 20 breaths/min. HEENT & skin: mild scleral icterus and multiple ecchymoses on the extremities.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC & smear: WBC 6,110/uL (4% bands, 77% segmented neutrophils, 7% lymphocytes, 6% normoblasts, 3% myelocytes), Hb 11.5 g/dL, platelets 3,000/uL. Chemistry & serology: total bilirubin 3.89 mg/dL (normal 0-1.3 mg/dL), ALP 480 U/L (normal 60-220 U/L), normal renal function, transaminases, and electrolytes; RF 76.3 IU/mL (normal <15 IU/mL), ESR 30 mm/h (normal 0-20 mm/h), CRP 100 mg/L (normal 0-5 mg/L); HIV and ANA negative. Chest radiograph: bilateral interstitial micronodules and fibrocalcified pattern. Abdominal ultrasound: splenomegaly.
objective.advanced_workup: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy: performed for refractory thrombocytopenia and leukoerythroblastosis, revealing intracellular yeast forms highly suspicious for disseminated histoplasmosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis presenting with severe thrombocytopenia mimicking methotrexate-induced myelosuppression. Confirmation: Bone marrow aspirate/biopsy cytology, bone marrow fungal culture growing Histoplasma capsulatum mold after 4 weeks, and PCR assay confirming H. capsulatum (peripheral blood and sputum fungal cultures were negative). Plan & clinical course: Treated with IV amphotericin B (0.7 mg/kg/day to a total cumulative dose of 1 g) with clinical improvement, then discharged on oral itraconazole 200 mg daily (discontinued after 2 weeks due to impaired liver function); remained relapse-free at 3-month follow-up.
